thread.title: Stocks Move To The Downside As Fed Announcement Looms - U.S. Commentary

title: Stocks Move To The Downside As Fed Announcement Looms - U.S. Commentary
text:
Stocks Move To The Downside As Fed Announcement Looms - U.S. Commentary May 02, 2018, 12:00:00 PM After initially showing a lack of direction, stocks have moved moderately lower over the course of the trading session on Wednesday. The major averages have all pulled back into negative territory after turning in a mixed performance earlier in the day.
Currently, the major averages remain in the red. The Dow is down 103.47 points or 0.4 percent at 23,995.58, the Nasdaq is down 17.32 points or 0.2 percent at 7,113.38 and the S&P 500 is down 10.67 points or 0.4 percent at 2,644.13.
The weakness that has emerged on Wall Street comes as traders are looking ahead to the Federal Reserve's monetary policy announcement this afternoon.
 interest rates unchanged, but traders will keep a close eye on the accompanying statement for clues about the outlook for rates.
The looming Fed announcement has largely overshadowed the release of a report from payroll processor ADP showing
"Despite rising trade tensions, more volatile financial markets, and poor weather, businesses are adding a robust more than 200,000 jobs per month," said Mark Zandi, chief economist of Moody's Analytics.
He added, "At this pace, unemployment will soon be in the threes, which is rarified and risky territory, as the economy threatens to overheat."
Despite the pullback by the broader markets, Apple ( AAPL ) is holding on to a strong gain after the tech giant reported fiscal second quarter results that beat analyst estimates on both the top and bottom lines.
Apple also said its board approved a new $100 billion share repurchase authorization and a 16 percent increase in its quarterly dividend.
Sector News
Most of the major sectors continue to show only modest moves, although considerable weakness has emerged among healthcare stocks.
Reflecting the weakness in the healthcare sector, the Dow Jones U.S. Health Care Index has fallen by 1.1 percent.
Telecom stocks have also shown a notable move to the downside on the day, dragging the NYSE Arca Telecom Index down by 1 percent.
On the other hand, oil service stocks are seeing significant strength in mid-day trading, with the Philadelphia Oil Service Index climbing by 1.1 percent.
The strength among oil service stocks comes despite a modest decrease by the price of crude oil, as crude for June delivery is slipping $0.13 to $67.12 a barrel.
Other Markets
In overseas trading, stock markets across the Asia-Pacific region turned in a mixed performance during trading on Wednesday. Japan's Nikkei 225 Index edged down by 0.2 percent, while Australia'sS&P/ASX 200 Index climbed by 0.6 percent.
Meanwhile, the major European markets all moved to the upside on the day. While the German DAX Index jumped by 1.5 percent, the U.K.'s FTSE 100 Index and the French CAC 40 Index rose by 0.3 percent and 0.2 percent, respectively.
In the bond market, treasuries have shown a lack of direction ahead of the Fed announcement. As a result, the yield on the benchmark ten-year note, which moves opposite of its price, is down by less than a basis point at 2.974 percent.
